scope_note: V-FINAL adversarial re-verification of the POST-RULING shipping bytes (candidates-final/elf-b14-001.json, written 2026-08-26 11:24 local). This file REPLACES the 2026-08-25 pre-repair audit; that audit's seven findings are carried below as resolved_findings or restated as live findings, and the superseded file remains in git history. Evidence read: the shipping bytes end to end; verdicts-ruling/{gkey-elf-r1,gkey-elf-r2,gkey-resolved,gdistractor,geng,gstem,gregister}.jsonl; ADJUDICATION.md sections elf-b14-001, AGARBLICK 1 and 4, and AGARDOM 2026-08-26; the pre-ruling G-STEM legs in verdicts/ and verdicts-regate2/; the git diff of the repaired file against HEAD. Independent work performed: full cold solve of all five items from the repaired passage alone before reading any key; byte-level diff of the repair; an independent mech re-run on the shipping bytes; token counts under gates/scripts/mech.py:tokenize; verbatim-citation check over all five rationales; sheet sync and contamination check; a bank-wide law-13 name grep; and a cross-question corroboration sweep over the stems sheet.
no_blocker_statement: No ship-blocker found. The three owner-ordered edits were applied exactly, exclusively and faithfully; no key moved; every gate leg run against the repaired bytes returns pass or flag with zero kills; and my own cold solve reproduces the recorded keys 5/5 with each key uniquely defensible. Everything below is minor, note or info.

cold_solve.method: Solved from the repaired passage alone, arguing every option in every item, before opening any key, rationale or verdict file.
reasoning: Q1 = B. P2: 'Wear is not spread evenly along the chain either. It gathers in the length that sweeps the ground and in the two or three links either side of the swivel'. B recasts both halves. A is denied by the same sentence's tail ('usually condemned on a single bad metre') and by 'not spread evenly'. C imports salt corrosion, a word the passage never uses. D, in its repaired wording, is still the paragraph-4 concession about POSITION worn as an answer about WEAR; 'channel' does not occur in the passage at all, and nothing says inshore chains wear harder.

Q2 = C. P2: 'wind and tide swing the buoy about its sinker, and the more chain it has, the wider the ground it can wander over, so the light is somewhere inside that circle rather than on the cross printed on the chart.' A hardens buoy 43's single 31-for-11 measurement into a district rule with 'must', which P4-P5 deny ('on the scope its master chose'); it also fails to answer the stem, which asks what is implied about displacement. B runs the arrow backwards, and the passage states the true direction twice (P2 mechanism; P4 'the buoys laid longest' are the ones measured off). D imports an early-lift policy the fixed three-year cycle never mentions. C alone survives, and 'may be' keeps it inside what the text licenses.

Q3 = A. The paragraph's load-bearing clause is 'because a moored ship does not sit still either and her keepers knew it', capped by Fewtrell's 'Where we were over it was another question.' The digression dates the position problem that Prigent's loggers now quantify. B is contradicted by 'does not sit still either'. C generalises one vessel's costed withdrawal into a coast-wide post-war decline the text never draws, and 'after the war' is not in the passage. D asks a different question (keeper attentiveness) and is not the writer's purpose.

Q4 = D. P4 closes 'Cadell has read the recordings and concedes the inshore aids, where the water is narrow. On the outer stations he has not moved.' A overshoots the partial concession into surrender. B substitutes a cost argument for the stated mechanical one ('it is the chain that fails'). C invents an origin for a practice the text attaches to no starting point.

Q5 = B. The piece is a day on the tender (lift, chain, scope, swing circle, wear, turnaround) with an argument about how much slack running through P4-P5 and left open ('Neither record disposes of the other'). A promotes one paragraph to the whole. C turns reported measurement into a recommendation the writer never makes. D tracks a cost thesis the text does not carry.

findings.check: rationale-option coherence on an edited span — Q1 WHY-DISTRACTORS still describes D by its pre-repair wording
findings.quote: D = wrong_location / surface_word_match -- 'inshore aids, where the water is narrow' is lifted from the paragraph-4 concession about position, not about wear
findings.note: The ruling changed option D but not the rationale line that argues it. The quoted string is verbatim passage, so this is not a fabricated citation, but the sentence is built as 'D's wording is lifted from paragraph 4', and D no longer contains 'water'. A student who reads D ('where the channel is narrow') and then the rationale ('where the water is narrow') sees two different strings presented as the same one. This is student-facing teaching payload, which is why I record it rather than filing it as metadata. The ARGUMENT is untouched and correct: D really does borrow the paragraph-4 concession about position and answer a question about wear, and generator_meta.self_blind_solve_post_ruling states D's new wording correctly. The repair_log's item (a) note addresses D's role, its trap label and its token count, but never asks whether any rationale quotes D. Fix is a four-word rewrite of that clause ('D borrows the paragraph-4 concession, "the inshore aids, where the water is narrow", which is about position, not wear'); it touches no option, key or stem and so triggers no blind re-gate. Recommended before bank import, not a blocker for the ruling round.

findings.check: the ordered repair trades one house-style minor for another (G-REGISTER, fresh leg)
findings.quote: the buoys laid longest sit as much as thirty-five metres from their charted places for hours together
findings.note: G-REGISTER passes the unit but records that the spell-out puts the passage above the authentic corpus's observed mid-sentence ceiling: across 140 authentic ELF passages the largest spelled-out cardinal in the article's own voice is 'twenty degrees above normal', and every measured quantity above that is in digits ('142 feet', '30 centimetres', '250 kilometres', '13,491 tonnes'). So the edit that discharged a 9-of-9 G-ENG flag opens a 1-of-1 G-REGISTER flag on the same span. I judge the trade net-positive and so does the gate: the pre-repair state rendered two same-unit measurements ('thirty-one metres', '35 metres') two different ways with no rule behind the split, whereas the post-repair state is rule-governed; the same charge already applied pre-repair to 'two hundred and fourteen floating aids', so the density of an existing choice rose rather than a new one appearing; and the unit declares a BrE literary quarterly, a real style family that spells out under a hundred, against a corpus of digit-heavy news and science monthlies. Recorded because an honest audit of an owner-ordered edit must state what the edit cost, not only what it bought.

findings.check: fresh G-ENG minor on the KEYED option of Q1 (leg 3)
findings.quote: It builds up where the chain drags on the bottom and close to the swivel.
findings.note: Unpunctuated coordination of unlike adjuncts: 'where the chain drags on the bottom' is a clause, 'close to the swivel' is a prepositional phrase, and the first reading can pull the phrase inside the where-clause, giving 'the chain drags both on the bottom and close to the swivel' — which is not the passage's mechanism. Not answer-affecting: under either reading B is the only option naming both ground contact and the swivel, and A, C and D stay false, so the item does not turn on the comma. One leg of three; the gate itself calls the intended reading 'the only sensible one'. The remedy is one comma, but a comma in an OPTION is an option edit and would re-open G-KEY x2 + G-DISTRACTOR under the runbook trigger, so it should ride a later editorial pass rather than a fourth unordered edit inside the ruling round.

findings.check: question style — bare deixis in the main-idea stem is off-corpus (G-REGISTER, new this round)
findings.quote: What is this text mainly about?
findings.note: Zero of 200 authentic ELF long-passage prompts contain 'this text'; all 24 authentic main-idea prompts name the writer, the article or the paragraph ('What is the writer's main point in connection with...', 'What overall conclusion concerning the NHS is drawn in the text?'). Bareness itself is corpus-legal ('Why is Leo Tolstoy mentioned?'), so this is a phrasing lean toward school-comprehension register, not a wrong question type. The gate records it and does not charge it. New on this unit's ledger, and untouched by the ruling repair. A prompt edit is a stem edit and would re-open the blind gates, so it belongs upstream as a generation law ('name the writer or the article in whole-text stems') rather than as a batch14 repair.

findings.check: residual defensibility route on Q3/D that the standing defence does not cover — raised and rejected
findings.quote: Her recordings put a figure on something the crews had only estimated
findings.note: My own hunt, not on any gate's record. The standing defence of Q3/D (G-DISTRACTOR ARGUABLE, 2026-08-25, defended not repaired) argues from the paragraph-3 causal clause. It does not address this paragraph-4 clause, which says the tender crews 'had only estimated' where the lightship keepers took 'three bearings taken on the shore marks' every watch and chalked a corrected position — material a determined candidate could assemble into 'the old keepers may have watched their position more closely than today's crews'. REJECTED on two independent grounds. (1) Different objects: the tender crews were estimating the BUOYS' excursion; the keepers were fixing THEIR OWN position. A tender crew is not on station and has no position of its own to keep, so the comparison the option asserts is not drawn anywhere in the text. (2) Wrong question: the stem asks why the WRITER mentions the lightship, and the paragraph states its own purpose in a causal clause ('because a moored ship does not sit still either and her keepers knew it'), closed by a quotation that says the keepers did NOT know where they were. D is a plausible-sounding proposition that is not the writer's purpose — which is exactly what a well-made purpose distractor is. The fresh G-DISTRACTOR leg returns pass on q:3 with zero findings, superseding the older ARGUABLE.

findings.check: escalated G-DISTRACTOR observation — repaired Q1/D and the clause where Q4's key lives — written disposition
findings.quote: It is heaviest on the aids moored inshore, where the channel is narrow.
findings.note: DISPOSITION: no repair, written disposition only. Measured rather than asserted. (i) The channel does not exist. Longest common word run between Q1/D and Q4/D is ONE token ('the'); the only shared content words are 'aids' and 'inshore'. Q4/D's discriminating content — that Cadell CONCEDED the inshore aids and has NOT moved on the outer stations — gets no corroboration whatsoever from Q1/D, which says nothing about concession, about Cadell, or about outer stations. (ii) It is not new. 'inshore' and the narrow-water adjunct were both in D before the ruling; the edit removed the word 'water' and nothing else, so the Q1/D-to-Q4/D conceptual adjacency is exactly as old as the unit. If anything the verbatim tie to the passage LOOSENED: longest common run between D and the passage fell from 3 tokens ('water is narrow') to 2. (iii) Charging it would abolish the trap class. wrong_location is defined as borrowing from a paragraph other than the one the stem is anchored in; in a five-question block every paragraph is some question's anchor, so any wrong_location distractor necessarily borrows from a sibling item's home paragraph. (iv) The blind evidence agrees. The fresh G-STEM leg read the whole sheet with options and no passage, hunted cross-question channels explicitly, FOUND and reported one (q:4 with q:5), and did not name this one; G-DISTRACTOR returns pass on both q:1 and q:4 with zero findings. CONCLUSION: a real adjacency, not a working leak; nothing beyond this written disposition is owed.

findings.check: cross-question route to eliminating Q2/B that no gate named — my own find, pre-existing surface
findings.quote: He has given it up since reading what Prigent's loggers recorded.
findings.note: Read as a sheet without the passage: q:4's stem establishes that Cadell 'lays his buoys long'; q:4/A establishes that Prigent's loggers RECORDED something that could make him give it up; q:2's stem establishes that buoy displacement from the charted position is the topic under discussion. A reader who links those three can infer that the loggers measured long-laid buoys as the displaced ones, which inverts and eliminates q:2/B without any physics. G-STEM reached the same elimination of B by the physical route and classified q:2 WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; this is a second route to the same place. NOT charged and NOT repair-caused: q:2 and q:4 options are byte-identical to the pre-ruling surface that three earlier G-STEM legs judged, it takes two inferential steps, and eliminating B still leaves A, C and D, so it does not decide the item — the residual path to C runs through the same domain knowledge the gate already flagged. Recorded so the next reviewer does not rediscover it as new.

findings.check: repair_log item (a) asserts a lure-tightening it does not demonstrate
findings.quote: the shortened form actually tightens the surface lure, since 'where the channel is narrow' sits one word from the passage span 'where the water is narrow'
findings.note: True as a claim about the syntactic frame ('where the [noun] is narrow'), and the one-word-apart description is literally accurate. But by the measure the program actually uses for surface lift, the lure loosened: longest common word run between Q1/D and the passage falls from 3 tokens ('water is narrow') to 2 ('it is'). Both statements can be true at once and neither affects the item; recorded at info so that the phrase is not later cited as a measured result. The same note's token arithmetic IS exact and I reproduced it: Q1 A(18) > B key(15) > C(14) > D(13, was 14) under mech.py:tokenize, so M-TELL's no-longest-key property holds.

gstem_dispositions.gate_result: flag / WORLD_KNOWLEDGE / blind pick B (= key)
gstem_dispositions.disposition: ACCEPT, no redesign. The lean is topical, not structural. A reader who knows that mooring-chain wear concentrates at the seabed touchdown sweep and at the swivel recovers B without the passage — but the gate's own record states there is 'no structural tell', that A, C and D are 'all substantively plausible passage claims', and that 'a reader without marine knowledge sees four parallel options'. The gate contract routes globally-true-key-plus-substantive-distractors to flag rather than kill precisely because authentic HP ELF items behave the same way: a biologist recovers keys from a biology passage. The lean is not even stable across readers — two of the four G-STEM legs ever run on this item called it clean. No repair is available that would not damage the item: making B false to the world would break the key, and weakening the distractors would create the structural tell the gate says is absent.

gstem_dispositions.gate_result: flag / WORLD_KNOWLEDGE / blind pick C (= key), plus a secondary 'mild test-wiseness tell'
gstem_dispositions.disposition: ACCEPT, no redesign. Two components, both answered. (1) Domain lean: the watch-circle account is the standard physical explanation for an off-charted buoy, and the same physics inverts B — which is the distractor doing its designed job, not leaking. This is the one flag that has been stable across all four legs, and every leg routed it to flag. (2) Shape tell: C is the only concede-and-reject option ('may be ... not ...'), but the gate itself grades it soft and gives the reason — the hedge count is 2-2 since the 2026-08-25 repair (C 'may be', B 'is likely to lie'), so 'pick the qualified option' scores at chance here. I add one route the gate did not name and reject it as a charge: q:4's stem plus q:4/A plus q:2's own stem let a sheet-only reader infer that long moorings are the displaced ones and so eliminate B, but that takes two inferential steps, rests on option surfaces the ruling repair did not touch, and still leaves A, C and D. Recorded in findings[] as a note; not a basis for redesign.

gstem_dispositions.gate_result: flag / PARTIALLY / blind pick A (= key), on a near-duplicate B/D pair plus an off-scope C
gstem_dispositions.disposition: ACCEPT, no redesign, with an upstream recommendation. The elimination path the leg describes is real: B and D both assert that the manned arrangement was better on position, so a test-wise reader discards them as mutually undermining, and C's 'after the war' frame is touched by nothing else on the sheet, leaving A. But this is leg variance, not a property the repair introduced and not a stable defect: q:3's stem and all four options are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the surface that three earlier G-STEM legs judged, and all three called it NOT_ANSWERABLE. Three of four legs clean. The only real remedy is a Q3 option-set redesign, which is outside the owner's ordered scope, would re-open a full blind re-gate on an item no gate has ever killed, and would risk regressing an item the passage supports cleanly. Carry it upstream instead as a generation law for batch16: purpose items should not carry two distractors that agree with each other.

gstem_dispositions.gate_result: flag / PARTIALLY / blind pick D (= key), on a q:5 cross-question channel plus a partial-concession shape tell
gstem_dispositions.disposition: ACCEPT, no redesign. Same leg-variance ground as q:3 and stronger: q:4's stem and all four options are byte-identical to the surface three earlier legs judged, and all three returned NOT_ANSWERABLE. The named channel is weak in both directions — q:5/B tells a sheet-only reader that the argument is UNSETTLED, which disfavours q:4/A because A settles it, but says nothing at all about B, C or D, so it eliminates one option out of four. The gate's own blind pick therefore rests on option shape ('the only two-part partial-concession option'), and it records its own confidence as low: 'B (cost defence) and C (storm origin) remain substantively live passage claims, so the item is not decided blind.' A shape heuristic that happens to land on the key is not a leak; if it were, no HP item could ever key a nuanced two-part answer.

gstem_dispositions.gate_result: flag / PARTIALLY / blind pick B (= key), on sibling-stem reconstruction plus a breadth tell
gstem_dispositions.disposition: ACCEPT, no redesign for batch14; recommend a generation law for batch16. This is the strongest flag in the sheet and I will not argue it away. B genuinely is reconstructible from the four sibling stems alone — q:1 chain wear, q:2 a buoy off its charted position, q:3 a marked position before loggers, q:4 'laying his buoys long' (i.e. slack) — and both halves of B are spelled out by them without the passage and without domain knowledge. My grounds for accepting anyway are three. (1) It is a property of the FORMAT, not of this unit: in any five-question long-passage block the four detail stems necessarily sample the passage, so the main-idea option that covers what they sample will always be the recoverable one. The gate says as much in its own calibration — 'a main-idea key being the broadest option is the ordinary shape of authentic HP main-idea items'. (2) It is pre-existing and owner-visible: the same flag stood in the ADJUDICATION package, was listed under AGARBLICK 4b, and the owner approved the batch-wide G-STEM point in the AGARDOM of 2026-08-26; the ruling repair touched neither q:5 nor any sibling stem. (3) The only genuine repair is to build q:5 a distractor with comparable stem coverage but a wrong thesis, which is a Q5 redesign — outside the ordered scope and a change the owner did not authorise. The right home for this is a batch16 law: in a 5q block, at least one main-idea distractor must cover the same sibling-stem span as the key.
